--- Page 1 (Beckerman_04a) --- Dear Folks, Ruth: Wrote to you a few times last week So was rather busy last week in writing this weeks. I have two letters around now of yours that I haven't answered. One came this morning. Thanks to the War Bond and also to the Benny Goodman article. Which reminds me that I would enjoy receiving newspaper clippings which you think might be of interest to me. She wrote that he stopped up to see you. He says he enjoys speaking to Mama very much. Perhaps I shall soon be in his shoes. I went to the beach on New Year's day (I had off) and had a great time. I think I already told you about the beaches in Aust. They're quite different from those at home. The waves, surf, I can see that you can stay and currents so you part of the day horse-back riding which I enjoyed immensely — except for the sore legs. --- Page 2 (Beckerman_04b) --- Very glad to know that you're kind of settled about Abe. His letters sound very realistic yet assuming. Too bad Papa isn't feeling his best again. Take good care of him till we get back. I can't entirely sympathize with you Ruth on exam cramming. It used to drive me almost crazy - but the exams were invariably easier than I had expected. Hope you have the best of luck and confidence with them - I know you will. And certainly am happy that you're going in for the farmculin - I didn't very much and regret it completely now. After college when people question you about your education - they'll always ask what you did besides studies. So keep up the good work. And on the history exam - just keep on writing until your name runs out (good old essay type question) into the exam. I can't remind you of the good expression. The current is my particular old mortgage. Thanks for your details. About Abe - Jack. Jack.
